transcript.text: The attack skill in RuneScape Dragon Wilds can seem a little bit more difficult to level than some of the
others since you're constantly in danger, but it is probably one of the most important and most widely useful
skills available. In this video, we'll talk about not just everything that you unlock with the attack skill, but why
it's useful and how to level it up as fast as possible. So, let's start off by talking about all the different things
that you unlock throughout the skill tree. To start out through all your in-between levels and everything after
40, you're going to get an extra 0.5% reduced stamina consumption when making melee attacks. At the beginning, this
has little to no impact, but as you start to level it up when you reach the higher levels, it allows you to make
several additional swings without having to stop to get more stamina. After that, at level five, you'll unlock
the ability to parry your opponent, which causes them to become staggered for a short period of time. This gives
you a big damage window and is also something they're planning to buff in the near future.
At level eight, you'll gain melee weapon special actions, which unlocks unique special actions for your melee weapons.
This is activated by middle mouse button on PC and allows you to do unique attacks depending on the weapon that
you're using. At level 11, you'll gain one of the most useful spells in the game, which is
Tempest Shield. This basically makes a huge wall of air in front of you anytime you're blocking and makes it so that you
take absolutely no damage as long as it's currently up when you block. They've actually set it up perfectly so
that as soon as the spell ends, it's able to be recast again. This not only prevents damage, though, but also allows
you to stun your enemies whenever they make an attack against you and it bounces off. Even better, this can
actually block range attacks when using weapons that are two-handed and you don't have access to a shield. At level
16, you'll unlock an additional attack for your melee weapon combos. This just lets you do more damage and get a little
bit extra out from each swing that you're getting in. At level 20, you'll gain your first
weapon enchant, which is enchant weapon fire. This not only does extra fire damage, but also applies the burning
debuff anytime you land a critical hit. At level 23, you'll gain adaptability, which makes it so evading or blocking no
longer interrupts your attack combos with melee attacks. This means that if you use it properly, you can start and
get two or three swings into your combo, do a dodge roll or a quick block, and then quickly finish off that attack
combo for the rewarding extra high damage final hit. At level 27, you'll simply gain the
ability to make a weapon rack where you can display all the weapons that you've collected. At level 30, you gain the
very best spell inside of the entire attack skill, which is enchant weapon air. This increases your attack speed
dramatically when using a melee weapon. I'll talk more about this later, but just know that this is by far and away
the best skill available to you. It makes it so that you're no longer stuck in animations for nearly as long, and
it's something you always want to be using. At level 34, you'll gain the ability to craft a lesser attack potion. This
grants you an extra 25% chance to land critical strikes while using melee weapons for the next 10 minutes.
At level 37, you gain the ability to craft a training dummy so that you can practice your combos and more
importantly figure out what weapon does the most damage. At level 40, you unlock the whetstone,
which just basically buffs all of the damage output for whatever melee weapon you're using. This is about 15% extra
damage, and it lasts for 10 full minutes, so you don't need to be using it very often, and they're very cheap to make.
And finally, at level 99, you'll get the infamous attack skill cape. And while it
doesn't actually have any crazy bonuses to it, it's still awesome to wear. All right. Now, let's take a quick
moment to talk about the best way to level your attack skill. And to be honest with you, this is going to vary
quite a bit depending on where you're at in the game. If you're very low level, to be honest, I would actually tell you
to probably focus more on your magic and range skill until you reach the second major biome. Once you get there, there's
a number of different things you can do, such as my personal favorite, which is going and farming the very first dragon
boss. He has a massive HP pool. You can pop XP pots and basically just farm him endlessly. You'll want to make sure
you're using the highest attack skill XP potion that you have available to you at
that time, which will probably be a 15%, but I'm guessing that if you're watching this video, you're more than likely
going to have the 30% one available, so use it if you have that option. Next, you'll want to make sure that you have
the inspiring amulet of attack, which provides a flat 5% XP boost while it's being worn. To top it off, make sure
that you're using any form of XP food that grants a 10% XP buff, as this is just another little boost. When all
combined, this should be giving you a total of 45% additional XP. Now, it's worth mentioning that if you have something
like the amulet of strength, which gives you a little bit of extra damage, it could be argued that that's actually
better than wearing the inspiring amulet of attack, at least if you're using end-game weapons. The main reason for
this is simply that by doing extra damage, you're gaining additional XP, as the harder you hit, the more XP you'll
gain. Now, if you don't want to farm the dragon, there's actually a few other spots that you can take advantage of. If
you've gotten towards the end of current content, you'll want to go ahead and try
the fight caves as a lot of people like to level in there. If you do go this route, I personally recommend that you
use an adamantite great sword and just spam your special attack as fast as you possibly can. As while you're doing
this, you'll be getting multiple hits and being able to stun lock enemies when done properly. Alternatively, if you're
past that first dragon boss, you will have the option to just go farm zombies as these are spawned pretty widely and
you can AoE them down and when some of them die, some will also respawn. There's of course also the option of
green dragons which just gives you a giant health pool, but I'm personally not a fan of these as they do take quite
a while to respawn and it just doesn't seem worth the travel time if you're trying to maximize your XP gains. With
that all out of the way though, let's talk about the different weapon types. You see, attack has really two different
types of attack damage. You have blunt damage and you have slashing damage. I personally would recommend that you
don't actually focus on this too much, but it is enough that it can be worth if you're in a zone with a lot of things
that are weak to blunt damage such as skeletons or knights that it might be worth you actually crafting a hammer
instead of a sword. My only reason I don't like the hammer is because when you use its special attack, it simply
stuns them and outside of that it is a very slow weapon. I would much rather be running either a one-handed mace and
shield or running a two-handed sword if I'm trying to level quickly because it can usually stun lock most low-level
enemies. So, it doesn't really matter what they're weak to. It is something to just keep in mind as slashing versus
blunt can be something that is very useful to you when used in the right context, but again, don't focus too much
on it. It's really not the most important thing in the world. Just know it's available. It's also worth
mentioning that there are actually other weapon buffs that you can give your weapon instead of a wetstone, such as
weapon barbs, weapon poison, and fire oil, which are all unlocked through different skill trees, but we'll go into
that on other skill tree videos, which you can check out if you'd like to see, as we'll be making skill guides on every
single skill available. With all of that in mind, let's actually talk about what is arguably the best gear available to
you currently within the game. First off, you're going to want to have a full set of adamantite armor. This is going
to give you the most damage resistance currently available, as well as give you all of the attack skill tier buffs for
wearing three different attack skill items. After that, you'll probably want to be running the amulet of strength,
although again, you can run an XP amulet or something else if you have a different preference or just don't have
access to this yet. Next, make sure that you're using a lesser attack potion if you're focusing on damage or running an
XP potion if you're focusing on leveling. And finally, I honestly think that the great sword is by far and away
the best weapon available, as all you need to do is spam middle mouse button, and most things will die. If you don't
like it though, you can of course choose whatever one you prefer, as this is about having fun and not min-maxing
every single possible thing. But, if you want to have what I think is the best gear in the game, any great sword will
do once you have them unlocked. mind that the great sword is not something you get access to right out of the gate,
so you might have to grind up a little bit in order to actually gain access to it. Lastly, I'll just let you know this,
and that is that the attack skill is actually the most complimentary skill to the other two that are available. You
really don't want to be running it by itself, and instead, I highly recommend that you run it alongside either ranged
or magic damage. That way, you have the ability to do a ranged attack or heal yourself through using water magic or
just have more AoE available to you. But, when you become overwhelmed and things are on top of you, you don't have
to stress too much as you've got all of that protective armor as well as having the ability to quickly kill things in
close combat faster than any other skill is currently able to do. Now, if you guys want to see more guides like this
one about how to not just level your skills, but also why they're useful and what you'll unlock in them, consider
checking out this video. I'm Game Advisor, and I'll see you in the next one.
